pr_title: Mention in docs about the query iteration order and result uniqueness.
pr_body:
# Objective
Fix #10876. Improve `Query` and `QueryState`'s docs.

## Solution
Explicitly denote that Query is always guaranteed to return results from all matching entities once and only once for each entity, and that iteration order is not guaranteed in any way.

issue_context.title: Query.iter does not indicate that it iterates over unique entities
comments:
For example, if `Filters` was `Or<With<ComponentA>, With<ComponentB>>`, one possible interpretation is that it will iterate over all entities with `ComponentA` followed by all entities with `ComponentB`, thus fulfilling the property that it will find every entity that fits the filter, but without fulfilling the property that it will find every entity at most once - it would find entities with both `ComponentA` and `ComponentB` twice.

Furthermore, even if Queries currently fulfill both properties (A: will find every entity in the World that fits the filters, and B: will find every entity at most once), since it is not documented, it is possible (if unlikely) that this may change. Documenting specifically that it is a logic error for either property to not be fulfilled will help prevent such a change from occurring.

review_comments: I was curious about this: Is the iteration order random at some length? Or do it choose as first some archetypes rather than others?

Right now it's in archetype ID order, but adding and removing components moves entities around both on tables and archetypes.

The exact iteration order should not be mentioned as it's not guaranteed in any form and subject to change at any time.
